bandReport.notes:
Q55-Q70, 16 questions, contiguous with no gaps. Printed page = index + 1 on all four pages (p18 = 19-A, p20 = 21-A, p22 = 23-A, p24 = 25-A), footer BFVS-T-TME throughout, confirming the config pre-pass.

BOTH SEAMS CLEAN. Opened p16 (printed 17-A) without transcribing it: it carries Q47-Q54 and Q54 completes on that page (stem plus all four options), so nothing is stranded before Q55. Opened p26 (printed 27-A) without transcribing it: it opens at Q71 with a fresh stem, so Q70 is not truncated. No Directions block and no shared-stimulus set straddles either seam.

NO SETS IN THIS BAND. The five data-sufficiency items Q61-Q65 each REPRINT the preamble in full, so they are standalone questions, not a set -- the same reading the config header records for the 2026-1 Q71-Q80 run. No question here carries context/setLabel.

OPTION (d) ACROSS THE DATA-SUFFICIENCY RUN -- the 2026-1 trap re-checked, and it does NOT reproduce. Every (d) was cropped from the source PDF at 6x and read on its own; none was copied between questions. All five read IDENTICALLY: 'The Question can be answered even without using both the Statements.' (Q61 p20 left, Q62 p20 right, Q63 p22 left, Q64 p22 right, Q65 p24 left). So on this paper the whole option block (a)(b)(c)(d) is constant across Q61-Q65, unlike 2026-1 where (d) alternated between 'cannot be answered even by using both' and 'can be answered even without using both'. Options (a),(b),(c) were also cropped and read independently for Q61 and Q62 at 4x and are word-for-word identical. NOTE the wording differs from the 2026-1 booklet in two places and is transcribed as printed here: this paper sets 'Statement I :' with a space (2026-1 set 'Statement-I :' with a hyphen), and closes with 'of the above Question and Statements ?' with no 'the' before Statements (2026-1 had 'Question and the Statements'). Verified at 5x.

ZERO FIGURES on all four pages, which corroborates the config's whole-paper survey rather than merely repeating it. Every geometry item in this band is prose-described (Q57 chord/minor segment, Q58 circular plate, Q59 octagon cut from a square, Q61-Q65, Q67, Q70) and no page carries a diagram, graph or table. No question in this band sets hasFigure.

ONE MISPRINT FLAGGED, Q60 option (d) -- see that question's flags.

questions.stem: A reservoir is in the form of a cuboid. Its length is 30 m. If 24 kL of water is removed from the reservoir, the water level goes down by 20 cm. What is the width of the reservoir ?
A well is dug with a diameter of 3.5 m and 16 m depth. The earth soil so excavated is spread in the form of a right circular cone of radius 7 m. What is the height of the cone ?
The chord of a circle is 20 cm and the height of the minor segment is 5 cm. What is the diameter of the circle ?
On a circular metal plate of uniform thickness, 16 holes, each of diameter 2 cm, are made. If the plate thereby has lost one-ninth of its original weight, then what is the diameter of the plate ?
A square of side length 4 cm has its corners cut away in such a manner so as to form a regular octagon. What is the length of the side of the octagon ? (Take \(\sqrt{2}\) = 1.41)

A tall cylindrical reservoir kept vertically is 20 m in diameter. Water is poured into it at the rate of 264 \(\text{m}^3\) per hour. What is the rate at which the water level rises in the reservoir per minute ? (Take \(\pi = \frac{22}{7}\))
flags: Option (d) prints '14 cm' with NO raised middle dot, while (a), (b) and (c) each print a single digit, a raised middle dot and a single digit (one point zero, one point two, one point four). Cropped from the source PDF at 7x and read again: (c) unambiguously carries the middle dot and (d) unambiguously does not, so this is not a scan artefact or a dropped dot in the render. Transcribed as printed. Flagged because a fourth option an order of magnitude away from the other three is the shape a dropped decimal separator takes, but the page does not support repairing it.
